definition: having a dislike or distrust of humankind
memoryTip: Mis + anthropos (human) — distrusts or dislikes people in general.
correctPassage: The character's misanthropic outlook colors every relationship in the novel.
wrongPassages: His misanthropic nature showed in weekly dinners for the whole neighborhood.
The misanthropic hostess thrived on large parties and constant guests.
She was so misanthropic that strangers always felt instantly welcomed.

definition: stubbornly uncooperative or resistant to authority
memoryTip: Re-calcitrant: digs in heels and kicks back — won't cooperate.
correctPassage: Recalcitrant members refused to accept the committee's compromise.
wrongPassages: The recalcitrant intern finished every task early and asked for more.
Recalcitrant voters lined up to support the bill without a single amendment.
Her recalcitrant attitude made her the easiest teammate to manage.

definition: lacking a plan or purpose; jumping from thing to thing
memoryTip: De-sultory leaps: hops around with no clear direction.
correctPassage: Their desultory efforts at reform produced little lasting change.
wrongPassages: His desultory study plan covered every chapter in careful order.
The desultory investigation followed a strict checklist from start to finish.
She gave a desultory presentation that never strayed from the outline.

definition: used for emphasis to mean genuine or true; real
memoryTip: Very + true — a genuine thing: a veritable flood of emails.
correctPassage: The archive is a veritable treasure of primary sources.
wrongPassages: The empty hall was a veritable throng of cheering fans.
Two lukewarm reviews made the film a veritable masterpiece overnight.
His veritable fortune consisted of three dollars and a broken watch.

definition: to faint or nearly faint from extreme emotion
memoryTip: Classic romance trope: so overwhelmed you almost faint.
correctPassage: Fans did not literally swoon, but the concert's energy was overwhelming.
wrongPassages: She managed to swoon through the entire lecture without losing focus.
He will swoon the spreadsheet by sorting every column twice.
The coach told them to swoon harder if they wanted to win the race.
